extracted.intended_audience: Presbyterian ministers, church officers, and members of the Covenanter/Scottish Presbyterian community
extracted.subtask_description: Official doctrinal and polity declarations of a Presbytery/Covenanter body setting standards on theology, church government, civil government, censures, oaths, and covenants. The page specifies what is to be affirmed and what errors/tenets are to be rejected or condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perseverance of the saints
rubrics_metrics.description: True believers, notwithstanding remaining corruption and various temptations and afflictions, must certainly and infallibly persevere in a state of grace unto the end, and be at last saved with an everlasting salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported by scriptural citations (Heb. xi.13; John iv.42; Phil. i.6; John x.28-29; 1 Pet. ii.9; Jer. xxxiv.4) and by the Confession (chap. 8, §1; chap.14 §2; chap.17).

rubrics_metrics.name: Liberty of conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Conscience is God's faculty in the soul and is not subject to human authority; human commands bind consciences only insofar as they agree with revealed will of God in matters of faith and practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although Christ has procured believers liberty from sin and ceremonial law, conscience is 'the rule ruled, not the rule ruling' — it does not license sinful lusts nor permit rejection or corruption of divine ordinances; deviation or mixing human inventions into scriptural institutions is disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Christian liberty and conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Conscience or Christian liberty cannot be used as a pretense to cherish forbidden lusts, reject divine ordinances, change or corrupt scriptural institutions, or deviate from their purity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations are sinful; those who espouse tenets contrary to established Christianity are accountable to the church and, upon conviction, may be proceeded against with ecclesiastical censures or civil pains as provided in Scripture and church order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toleration condemned
rubrics_metrics.description: It is wicked for any earthly power to tolerate by civil law the publication and propagation, with impunity, of errors, heresies, and damnable doctrines; toleration is destructive of true religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Toleration undermines the liberty Christ has given his people and the peace and order established in the church; citations include James iv.12; Rom. xiv.4; Acts iv.19; and Confession chap.20; catechism references offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testimony-bearing and communion of believers
rubrics_metrics.description: All true believers are savingly united to Christ and have communion with him in grace and glory; they share each other's gifts and graces and are bound to exercise commanded duties to preserve love of God and life of grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirmed with scriptural references (e.g., 1 John i.2-3; Eph. iii.16-19; Heb. x.24-25) and used to ground mutual responsibility within the visible church.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visible church obligations and covenantal faithfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: The visible church and its members are externally in covenant with Christ, profess the same faith, receive same seals (baptism and the Lord's Supper) and are bound to hold fast the Head, keep the faith, and maintain holy communion in worship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members may not recede from any part of divine truth they have professed without breach of duty; supported by scripture and catechism references (Acts ii.42; Eph. iv.4-6; Confess. chap.2,6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Christ as sole Head of the church
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lord Jesus Christ is the sole and supreme Head, Lawgiver, and King of his church; office-bearers derive mission and authority from him alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Christ commits keys of doctrine, government, discipline, and ordination to the church's officers; citations include 1 Cor. xii.28; Eph. iv.11; Matt. xviii.18-19; Acts xv.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office-bearers' authority and duties (keys)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordained office-bearers are entrusted (by Christ) with keys: to discover doctrine, preserve order and purity, inflict ecclesiastical censures, and ordain or set apart officers after suitable trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They exercise doctrine, government, discipline, and ordination as Christ's delegates, with scriptural support and reference to the church's directories and acts (e.g., 'Directory for electing of ministers').

rubrics_metrics.name: Presbyterian church government as sole warranted form
rubrics_metrics.description: The only ecclesiastical government warranted by Christ is presbyterial government: a connected judicative system of kirk-sessions, presbyteries, provincial synods, national assemblies, and ecumenical councils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This government is distinct from civil government and not subordinate to civil rulers; asserted as divinely warranted and unalterable in the church.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications and call of ministers and officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Office-bearers must evidence the qualifications required in Scripture and ministers must enter office by the door of Christ's appointment — by call and choice of the Christian people after suitable judgment of gifts and qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Qualifications drawn from 1 Tim. iii; Tit. i; Acts vi; and consistent with acts and ordinances of the reformation and discipline books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divine institution of civil government
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil government and magistracy are ordained by God for the preservation of peace, administration of justice, defense, encouragement of good, and punishment of evildoers; God is the supreme fountain of all power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations include Prov. viii.15-16; Rom. xiii.1-4; Deut. xvii.14; Confess. chap.23 §1, and parliamentary acts referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual and voluntary constitution of rulers and ruled
rubrics_metrics.description: The relation between rulers and ruled is voluntary and mutual: lawful constitution of magistrates is by mutual election of the people and consent of those elected, with stipulations according to Scripture and right reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only such a constitution can be approved by God; references to law and coronation oath practices cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of Christians toward lawful magistrates
rubrics_metrics.description: Christians are bound to pray for, reverence, esteem, conscientiously obey, defend and support lawful magistrates in due exercise of their power, especially in outward defense of the church and restraint of blasphemers and heretics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligation limited to lawful commands; scriptural references include 1 Tim. ii.1-2, 1 Peter ii.17, Rom. xiii.2-4.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of magistrates to the church
rubrics_metrics.description: Magistrates should use civil power to corroborate the laws and ordinances of Christ's house, ensuring that all in God's house is done according to God's law and protecting the church from external enemies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited historical oaths and acts, and scriptural supports (2 Kings xviii.4; Ezra vii.23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject opening communion to the grossly unfit
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the latitudinarian tenet of opening communion or sealing ordinances to the grossly ignorant, careless, profane, scandalous, anti-Christian deists, blasphemous heretics, or those holding doctrines contrary to fundamental Christianity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such inclusion is destructive to truth and holiness, spoils church purity and union; supported by Eph. v.11; 2 Cor. vi.17-18; references to historic church practice in exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject that God left church government unspecified
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the principle that God has left professing people without any declaration of his will concerning institution, administration, and qualifications for those who administer church ordinances, or that church government is left to human discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a notion is impious and contradicts 2 Tim. iii.16; Rom. ii.14; Confess. chap.23 §3; church discipline and pattern are claimed to be revealed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject papal and hierarchical headship
rubrics_metrics.description: Condemn the ecclesiastical headship arrogated by the Pope of Rome and the superiority of dignity and hierarchical order claimed by prelates, as usurpations contrary to Christ's sole headship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This hierarchical claim is said to elevate ministers contrary to Scripture and the nature of their office; citations include Psa. ii; Col. i.18; Confess. chap.25 §6.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject Erastian claim of civil supremacy over church
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the principle that the civil magistrate is supreme head over persons and causes ecclesiastical as well as civil (Erastianism), whether openly usurped or more craftily claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This encroaches on Christ's headship and has led to many practical encroachments; contrary to the church's covenants and reformation acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject civil control of ecclesiastical office power and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the tenet that any part of the power, mission, qualifications, or administration of ecclesiastical officers depends on the authority or dictation of the civil magistrate (e.g., prescribing tests, indulgences, oaths, or restricting mission).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such civil prescriptions are labeled gross Erastianism and destructive of ministerial freedom and the church's intrinsic power derived from Christ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject dependence of church government on magistrate will
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the opinion that the external government of Christ's house is precariously determined by sinful men or depends immediately/mediatedly on the civil magistrate's will and pleasure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is called an impious reflection on Christ's wisdom and leads to spiritual tyranny and disorder; scriptural citations provided (Exod. xxv; Ezek. xliii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject notion that Christ left no particular form of government
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the latitudinarian tenet that the Lord Jesus left his house without any particular form of government exclusive under the New Testament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a view is a reflection on Christ's faithfulness; Scripture and church propositions for government assert a revealed form (Confess. chap.30 §1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject kirk-session equality with superior judicatory
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the sectarian principle that a kirk session or particular congregational eldership holds equal ecclesiastical power with any superior judicatory and is not subordinate or accountable to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a stance undermines needed recourse to superior judgment and has been hurtful to church order; Acts xv and related citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject laity's public teaching/judicative authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the opinion that the community of the faithful in private stations has scriptural warrant for public teaching or judicative determination in the church.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This opinion is contrary to scripture and dangerous to the ministry and church order (Acts xv; 1 Cor. v; 1 Tim. v).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject intrusion of popish patronages
rubrics_metrics.description: Condemn the invasion and encroachment upon the church's liberties by the intrusion of popish patronages (whether civilly imposed or ecclesiastically executed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patronages are viewed as destructive of mutual relation between pastor and people, leading to schism and spiritual leanness by thrusting in unfit ministers; citations include John x; Heb. v; 1 Tim. iii.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject grounding magistracy in 'light of nature' instead of Scripture
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the anti-scriptural principle that the divine scriptural ordinance of magistracy is founded in the subjective light of nature rather than the moral preceptive law of God revealed in Scripture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural light (corrupted) is inadequate to reveal the true nature, use, and ends of God's ordinances; contrary to Deut. xvii; Ezek. xliii.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject non-Christian magistrates as sufficient constitution
rubrics_metrics.description: Reject the opinion that the election and choice of any person, however Pagan, Papist, Atheist, Deist, or enemy to God, by the civil body, by itself suffices to constitute a lawful magistrate according to God's ordinance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such a tenet contradicts scripture and reason and depreciates the contending of ancestors for civil reformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject that providentially acknowledged magistrates are necessarily preceptive
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclaim the notion that magistrates who happen to be providentially permitted or acknowledged in apostate/backsliding lands are necessarily preceptive (i.e., their authority preceptively binding in itself).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This view is contrary to scriptural precepts and tends to invalidate constitutional and covenant principles of reformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject explicit acknowledgment or obedience to anti-scriptural authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Testify against and condemn giving explicit acknowledgement, implicit subjection, or voluntary acts that imply approbation (praying for success, swearing oaths of fidelity, accepting office, military service) to anti-scriptural, anti-covenanted, Erastian governments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such actions are seen as homologation of unlawful authority and cannot be performed without deliberate approbation; historical context of persecution and Revolution referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemn voluntary payment or tribute to unlawful powers for conscience sake
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppose direct and active voluntary paying of tribute and dues unto such powers (when required as a test of loyalty or to accomplish wicked ends), when such payments evidence support for wicked authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include additional cess imposed during persecution to suppress preaching; contrasted with necessary lawful dues; scriptural and historical references provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject ministerial or church communion with unqualified or apostate ministers
rubrics_metrics.description: Testify against communion with those who occupy office but lack scriptural qualifications, enter office improperly, own another head than Christ, or apostatize — oppose attending their ministrations or receiving ordinances from them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such ministers are denied the Lord's blessing; congregants and ministers are to avoid active owning or countenancing of corrupt official ministrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject paying tithes to prelates/curates as due to lawful ministers
rubrics_metrics.description: Oppose voluntary contracting with prelates, curates, or invented officers for paying tithes or dues unto them as if they were lawful scriptural parish ministers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that under the New Testament priesthood change, tithes are not due to such officers; references 2 Cor. vi.17; Rev. ii.20 and historical acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths and vows are lawful parts of worship when proper
rubrics_metrics.description: Oaths and vows are part of religious worship, warranted in Scripture under the New Testament, and may be lawfully taken when lawful both in matter and manner; once engaged they must not be violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The right to administer oaths belongs only to those vested with authority agreeable to the word; lawful oaths include solemnly binding oneself to maintain and defend righteous rulers; disapproval only applies to oaths to unlawful authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to administer oaths limited to proper authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of administering oaths is competent only to those vested with such authority as is agreeable to the word of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes proper jurisdiction for oath administration and links lawful oaths with the duty of Christians to bind themselves to defend righteous rulers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disapprove refusing allegiance to lawful authority
rubrics_metrics.description: While rejecting oaths of allegiance to unlawful Erastian governments, the Presbytery disapproves the principle of refusing allegiance to lawful authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes lawful allegiance (appropriate to righteous rulers) from refusing allegiance where rulers are unlawful or anti-covenanted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condemn superstitious or profane forms of swearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Testify against profane and superstitious practices of swearing — e.g., laying hand on and kissing the gospels (as practiced in England/Ireland), unnecessary oaths at customs or trade, and secret-society oaths (Free Masons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These practices are labeled profanation or superstition and contrary to Scripture (Deut. x.20; Exod. xx.7; Neh. xiii.25; Confess. chap.22).

rubrics_metrics.name: National covenanting and solemn league binding
rubrics_metrics.description: The work of solemn covenanting with God in Christ is warranted by Scripture for individuals, churches, and nations; the National Covenant of Scotland and the Solemn League and Covenant are of divine authority and perpetually binding upon nations and posterity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covenants, once lawfully entered, are sacred and inviolable; opposition to national covenanting under the New Testament is rejected; scriptural references and examples (Deut. xxix; Gal. iii.15) provided.
